subject: Synapse - IP & Training Scope — redlines and decision log
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@synapse.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Ruiz <tom.ruiz@synapse.com>, legal@synapse.com
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Synapse MSA - redlines focused on training & output ownership

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team ran a pass on the MSA and order form and attached a consolidated redline (Synapse_MSA_redlines.pdf). The main asks from our side are narrow but material for our product/compliance team:

- Explicitly prohibit Redwood from using Customer Content or Customer Outputs to train models used beyond Synapse (we asked for a training opt-out that survives termination).
- Customer wants output ownership/assignment language for outputs produced by the Service that are derived from Customer Content.
- Clarify feedback license: Synapse will share operational telemetry and limited prompt/response pairs but only under a one-way, non-exclusive license for quality improvement, not for model re-release or commercialization.

We tried to mark fallback language that would be acceptable to both sides (see redline page 4). Can you route this to your legal/product team and share your suggested compromise language? We are on a tight procurement timeline (closing target 6/10).

Attaching a short spreadsheet with line-item priority (synapse_redline_comments.xlsx). If it helps I can do a 30-min call with your counsel this Thursday afternoon.

Regards,
Sarah Park
Head of Procurement | Synapse Systems

From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Synapse MSA - redlines focused on training & output ownership

Forwarding Synapse's redlines. TL;DR of asks and our constraints below — would appreciate legal + product guidance so I can push back with one consolidated proposal.

Quick summary:
- Training opt-out that survives termination (customer wants explicit prohibition on using Customer Content/Outputs in models that are available outside their tenancy).
- Output ownership: they want assignment or a broad warranty that outputs are "Customer-owned" when derived from Customer Content.
- Feedback license: limited, non-commercial license for product improvement only; no permission to publish, re-release, or train public models.

Our constraints:
- We currently rely on anonymized feedback + aggregated telemetry to tune system-level improvements. Removing that could significantly impact our long-term model quality pipeline and cost assumptions.
- Operationally, we can offer a per-account opt-out and stricter controls in Dedicated/Private offers; hosted customers making this ask are trickier for our product roadmap.

Requested help:
1) Laura — sample compromise language we can offer on training opt-out and durable obligations post-termination.
2) Marcus — can product commit to technical controls (logical isolation, separate training flags) for Synapse's account if legal accepts limited carveouts?
3) Monica — note any procurement/Sales motion updates (credits, timeline) if we take a conservative stance.

I plan to propose an interim approach: limited training opt-out (no use for generalized model training) + allow narrow, scoped usage for internal model improvements under strict aggregation/anonymization and with a contractual prohibition on re-release/commercialization.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call with Laura and Synapse counsel if that speeds things up.

Best,
Jasmine
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0193]

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 13:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Synapse MSA - redlines focused on training & output ownership

On Tue, May 30, 2028 at 11:08 AM Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com> wrote:
> Forwarding Synapse's redlines. TL;DR of asks and our constraints below — would appreciate legal + product guidance so I can push back with one consolidated proposal.

Thanks for the clear summary, Jasmine. High-level thoughts: we should avoid language that looks like an assignment of IP for Outputs across the board — that creates license and indemnity downstream. Instead:

- Output ownership: Offer a warranty and license structure. Proposed language: "Customer retains ownership of Customer Content. Redwood grants Customer an exclusive, perpetual license to Outputs to the extent such Outputs are reproducible and derived solely from Customer Content; otherwise Redwood retains ownership of service outputs." (I will draft a redline snippet.)

- Training/use of Customer Content: Agree to a durable opt-out: "Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to train or improve models used outside Customer's dedicated environment; any aggregated, de-identified telemetry used for product improvements will exclude Customer Content per this Section." That tracks procurement ask but preserves our ability to use aggregated telemetry if we can certify de-identification.

- Feedback license: Propose a one-way, non-exclusive, limited-purpose license: "Customer may provide Feedback; Customer hereby grants Redwood a limited, non-exclusive, non-transferable license to use such Feedback solely to operate, maintain and improve the Redwood service and not for sale or re-release as a model for third parties." Add a representations line that Synapse will not provide highly sensitive datasets as Feedback.

Open questions for product: How quickly can we enforce a per-account opt-out in hosted? If For Dedicated/Private we can provide stronger guarantees in the offering and pricing.

I'll attach a redline snippet in a follow-up (legal redline: suggested language under Sections 3.1 and 5.2). If Synapse insists on assignment of Outputs, we should push for a limited carveout (e.g., "Outputs that are mere transformations of Customer Content").

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com

[Draft redline to follow]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 01 Jun 2028 15:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Synapse - IP & Training Scope — redlines and decision log

Thanks — quick operational answers from Product/Engineering:

- Hosted: we can implement an account-level opt-out flag that prevents ingestion of Customer Content into model training pipelines, and mark any derived outputs as "opted-out" in telemetry. That would require a 6-week rollout and coordination with infra (we can prioritize for Synapse if this deal is timeboxed).

- Dedicated/Private: we can provide contractual guarantees and technical isolation earlier — Dedicated customers can ensure no cross-tenant training. For Private, full isolation is standard. Pricing impact: opt-out for hosted is +10–20% per token cost (since caching/batching opportunities reduce), Dedicated/Private would be priced separately.

- Auditability: we can provide quarterly attestations that Synapse data was excluded from training sets and a one-time export of telemetry artifacts used for product improvement upon request (redact identifiers).

Recommended next steps:
1) Laura to send the redline snippet and a short memo with the proposed warranty/license language.
2) Jasmine to present a single negotiation position to Synapse: (a) durable training opt-out for hosted + opt-in for aggregated de-identified telemetry; (b) limited Outputs license (not full assignment); (c) feedback license limited to product improvement and no re-release. Include pricing delta and timeline.
3) If Synapse declines, offer Dedicated/Private route with contractual guarantees.

Happy to jump on a call with Synapse counsel Thurs 6/1 if that helps.

Marcus Lin
Director, Product Management | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com

[Sent from Redwood HQ — attachment: product-impact-summary.xlsx (attached to internal folder)]
